synopsis: Heavy machines combine service brakes, drivetrain retarders and, on many machines, hydrostatic slowing; deployed intervention approaches differ, ranging from Toyota SEnS+ power shutoff to Liebherr hydrostatic stopping and Hexagon retarder/service-brake intervention [f13744, f1407, f1648, f1663]. Retarder deceleration is power-limited, declining with speed and mass and further reduced downhill; historic haul-truck studies reported 1–2 seconds of lag, but these are not valid design constants for a 2027 system [f5994, f5897, f6063]. Braking models should represent state-dependent actuator blending and hydrostatic capacity rather than a constant or single pedal-to-torque gain, because ignoring hydrostatic slowing can trigger collision intervention too early or too late [f6048, f6049, f6050, f6145]. ISO 3450 separates service, secondary and parking functions, and hydrostatic slowing cannot substitute for parking braking; meanwhile, no US federal construction or mining rule requiring automatic service-brake intervention after an ignored warning was found [f13746, f6544, f2247]. Higher-fidelity modeling is targeted at hydraulics and latency, articulated/high-center-of-gravity stability, hydrostatic capacity and deformable ground, but modern production brake-delay distributions and recent hydrostatic modeling evidence remain gaps [f5906, f6551, f6446].
